identity.title: ALMA observations of lensed Herschel sources: testing the dark matter halo paradigm
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We carried out a pilot study of the lensing statistics of submillimetre-selected sources by making observations with the Atacama Large Millimetre Array (ALMA) of a sample of strongly-lensed sources selected from surveys carried out with the Herschel Space Observatory.

question.value: Can the standard dark-matter halo paradigm, with halo mass functions and density profiles from simulations including baryons, reproduce the observed distribution of image separations of Herschel-selected lensed submillimetre galaxies?

evidence.quote: We attempted to reproduce the distribution of image separations for the lensed sources using a halo mass function taken from a numerical simulation which contains both dark matter and baryons.

analysis_steps.goal: Measure Einstein radii from ALMA images

method.value: Einstein radii measured directly from images; for arcs a circle was fitted to emission peaks >4 sigma with uniform weighting; checked against preliminary lens models

evidence.loc: 2 The Pilot Sample and the ALMA Observations
evidence.quote: In cases where only an arc is visible (e.g HeLMS J001615.8+032435) a rough estimate of the Einstein radius was performed by fitting a circle to the peaks of the emission $( > 4\sigma)$.

validation.value: Compared with preliminary lens models, agreement confirmed

evidence.loc: 2 The Pilot Sample and the ALMA Observations
evidence.quote: The Einstein radii were measured directly from the images and subsequently compared with the respective values that arise from preliminary lensing models of these system, whereupon an agreement was confirmed.

method.value: Strong-lens statistics: halo mass function times volume element times cross-section for mu>=2, normalised; EAGLE, SIS and SISSA profiles with NFW outside transition masses

evidence.quote: We adopt the standard formalism for computing lensing statistics (cite: TurnerOstrikerGott1984), where we consider a population of dark-matter halos that act as deflectors
We calculated the cross section using a minimum magnification factor of $\mu_{min} = 2$.

key_parameters.value: halo-to-stellar mass ratio 30 for SISSA; z_lv = z_l or 2.5

evidence.quote: adopt a constant ratio of halo to stellar mass of 30

assumptions.value: Spherically symmetric lenses; flat LCDM with Omega_m=0.307, h=0.693

evidence.quote: We always assume that the lens is spherically symmetric, since ellipticity does not significantly affect the statistics of image separations

analysis_steps.goal: Fit transition masses to observed distribution

method.value: chi^2 minimisation against normalised observed histogram with Poisson errors; 100 Gaussian resamplings of measured separations for uncertainties

evidence.quote: we perform 100 simulations for each measurement by resampling each value at random from a Gaussian distribution with a standard deviation equal the value’s error.
In our analysis we decided to exclude the object J141351.9-000026
by performing a standard $\chi^2$ minimisation method

results_numeric.quantity: Sample size needed to distinguish density profiles

evidence.quote: we estimate that a sample of $\sim 500$ would be required for this distinction to be made possible.

findings_qualitative.value: 15 of 16 ALMA-observed sources show clear lensing features

evidence.quote: Out of these sources, 15 show clear evidence of lensing features.

claims.hypothesis: Simulation-based halo mass function and profiles reproduce the observed image-separation distribution
claims.experiment: Compared predicted normalised distributions (EAGLE, SIS, SISSA) with ALMA and SMA samples
claims.result: All three profiles agree with the observed distribution; SIS and SISSA need an upper transition mass ~1e13 Msun
claims.finding: Standard dark-matter halo paradigm is consistent with the data

evidence.quote: We found that we could reproduce the observed distribution with all three density distributions

claims.hypothesis: Virialization redshift affects the transition masses
claims.experiment: Fitted with z_lv = z_l and z_lv = 2.5
claims.finding: No evidence supports such a low transition mass

evidence.quote: However, there is still no evidence to support such a low-transition mass between galaxies and clusters.

why_this_data.value: ALMA has better resolution and surface-brightness sensitivity than SMA, so lensing arcs are not missed

evidence.loc: 2 The Pilot Sample and the ALMA Observations
evidence.quote: ALMA has much better angular resolution and surface-brightness sensitivity than the SMA, making it a much better instrument for mapping a strongly-lensed submillimetre source.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Oguri (2006b) two-component profile not used because the sample is too small to distinguish models

evidence.quote: However, as our sample is still limited in numbers to make such distinctions between models, we have not considered this approach.

limitations_admitted.value: Sample too small to distinguish density profiles; magnification bias not corrected

evidence.quote: we have decided not to do this because the luminosity function for submm sources is still very poorly constrained

referee_caveats_inferred: Einstein radii of arcs are rough estimates
